evaluations.verdict: A wins narrowly through stronger visual polish, clearer action, and safer integration identifiers. Both are high-quality, fully recognizable SVGs.

scores.label: A
strengths: Clear pelican-on-bicycle narrative with convincing wing, feet, pedals, and handlebar contact.
Balanced composition, cohesive palette, and refined layered strokes.
Prefixed IDs, resolved references, accessible title/description, and self-contained markup.
weaknesses: Fixed width and height reduce host-layout flexibility.
Repeated stroke-built anatomy and limited reusable classes make editing somewhat laborious.

scores.label: B
strengths: Immediately recognizable subject with strong silhouette and lively coastal setting.
Responsive viewBox-only root and useful shared stroke classes.
Well-organized groups, reusable definitions, and complete accessible labeling.
weaknesses: Leg, crank, and frame intersections are visually awkward and weaken the riding pose.
Generic IDs such as title, desc, sky, and shadow risk collisions when embedded repeatedly.
Blurred ground shadow and several heavy outlines feel less controlled than A.
